metadata.title: Broadcom Shares Fall 5.6% Even as Revenue Surges 86%

content.text:
This article first appeared on GuruFocus.
Broadcom (NASDAQ:AVGO), the AI-chip and infrastructure-software powerhouse, tumbled 5.64% to $346.54 on Thursdayeven after quarterly revenue rocketed 86%. A separate Reuters report exposed the problem. The quarter was huge. The bar was brutal. The stock paid the price.
Broadcom's third-quarter release delivered $29.59 billion in revenue, including $16.7 billion from AI semiconductors. Free cash flow surged to $13.67 billionan extraordinary 46% of sales. Management expects fourth-quarter revenue of approximately $34.8 billion, with AI-chip sales jumping to roughly $21.7 billion. Those are blockbuster numbers. Wall Street wanted fireworks on top of fireworks.
AI chips could climb from 56.4% of third-quarter revenue to approximately 62.4% next quarter, with the business expanding nearly 30% sequentially. But the valuation picture flashes a warning: Broadcom's $346.537 share price sits just 1.4% below its $351.46 GF Value, leaving almost no cushion for a merely excellent quarter. The AI engine is roaring. The cash machine is humming. Yet when perfection is already priced in, even spectacular growth can land like a disappointment.
